title: Inspect and extend: Share and save reports, messages, and settings
objective: Use the real implementation in `src/store.ts` to demonstrate and safely improve context initialization, asyncstorage adapter, store keys, hydration and effects.
problem: The provider is the app-wide coordinator and the store is its persistence seam. Follow load and save for the three stored domains and inspect malformed-data recovery tests. Your implementation or debugging result must remain consistent with the source architecture.
requirements: Read `src/store.ts` and the related project files: src/expenseContext.tsx; src/store.ts; App.tsx.
Add or improve a focused behavior related to context initialization, asyncstorage adapter, store keys, hydration and effects.
Add a meaningful unit test or, when platform tooling is unavailable, document a reproducible manual check.
Update documentation to identify local, simulated, external, and missing behavior accurately.
constraints: Do not claim or implement as complete a capability outside this boundary: AsyncStorage is local, unencrypted key/value persistence; it is not financial-grade secure storage.
Do not add credentials, personal records, real funds, or unsafe public network exposure.
Keep the change within the existing project architecture and name any new dependencies.
expected_behavior: The provider is the app-wide coordinator and the store is its persistence seam. Follow load and save for the three stored domains and inspect malformed-data recovery tests.
acceptance_criteria: The implementation change is traceable to `src/store.ts`.
Normal and failure/edge cases are described and tested.
The test outcome and environment are recorded honestly.
README or source comments correctly state remaining limitations.
hints: Read the caller and the closest existing test before editing.
Separate a pure rule test from any UI, device, provider, or network test.
